items.tip: Hear each syllable clearly. The Holy Name and Krishna are non-different — hearing IS the chanting.
If the mind wanders, return to the Name gently. Don't fight the wandering — that fight is also distraction.
Sit in one place. Begin slowly. Let the rhythm of breath find the rhythm of the Name.
Today, listen for the Name reaching back. Japa is a meeting, not a recitation.
Begin in the mood of service, not duty. Today's japa is offered, not performed.
Bhakti is its own reward. Chant without seeking — even without seeking peace.
Remember: I am not the doer. The Holy Name does the work. You are present.
Sixteen rounds is your standing vow. Today, begin where you are. The rest follows.
If yesterday slipped, today is not yesterday. The vow is renewed each morning.
A small vow kept is greater than a large one broken. Begin with what you can hold.
Today is Ekadasi. Begin japa earlier; complete before noon if possible.
Faith is not a feeling. It is the act of beginning anyway, when feelings are absent.
Today's japa does not require certainty. It requires presence.
Shraddha grows by chanting, not before. Begin.
Today's chanting was helped by what you heard yesterday. Tomorrow's hearing will be helped by today's chanting.
Carry one line from yesterday's SB class into japa. Let it return to you.
Hearing is the seed; chanting is the flower. Neither grows alone.
Clean body, clean place. Sit straight. The form is also offered.
Wash hands and mouth before beginning. Small acts make a clean approach.
Today's beads are also Krishna's. Hold them in the right hand, in the bag.
Before japa, remember the class you heard this morning. The hearing comes through your guru to you.
The guru's gift is the Name. To chant is to receive that gift again, daily.
Today's tip is not from this app. It comes through Prabhupada's books. Read them when you can.
If Tulasi is near, offer respects before japa. Her presence sweetens the Name.
Today, water Tulasi if you can. Even a drop.
Attention is the price of japa. Pay it gladly — the merchandise is priceless.
If you notice inattention, do not despair. Noticing IS the return.
Today, do not count rounds completed. Count rounds you heard.
Offer the result of japa to Krishna before chanting. The seed becomes a flower.
Surrender is not collapse. It is alignment.
Krishna chants through you. Step back and let it happen.
Japa is service. So is everything else. Today, do both with the same hand.
Family responsibilities are not interruptions to bhakti — they are the field of it.
Serve Krishna by serving those Krishna has placed near you.
Prema is the destination, not the start. Today, begin with shraddha and trust the path.
The chanter who finishes 16 rounds with love is greater than the chanter who finishes 64 with pride.
On Ekadasi, the Holy Name is especially powerful. Hear with full attention.
Today, no grains. Chant more. The fast feeds the chanting.
On Ekadasi, the mind is lighter. Begin japa with one extra round if you can.
Before counting beads, name one inner obstacle (anger, lust, greed, pride). Chant in spite of it, not around it. The Name purifies what is offered to it.
When the mind drags toward a worry, do not fight it — return to the Name once. That returning IS japa.
If shraddha feels weak today, do not delay japa for its return. Chanting is itself the cure.
Hear Hare and Krishna both — neither name alone. Hare invokes Sri Radha; Krishna invokes the Lord. The mantra unites them.
Today, give attention to the word 'Hare' on every line. It addresses the energy that introduces you to Krishna.
If you spoke critically of a Vaishnava this week, today's japa carries extra weight. Chant slower. Apologize inwardly first.
Do not chant to receive material results. Desire the Name for its own sake; everything else follows as a side effect.
Inattentive chanting (pramada) is itself the tenth offense. Notice the wandering — that noticing IS attention.
Today, remember the guru through whom this Name reached you. Hear with that gratitude.
Sit with the spine straight. Cross the legs simply. The body offered straight steadies the mind.
Hold the beads in the right hand inside the bead-bag. The thumb and middle finger pass each bead. The index finger does not touch the beads.
Do not cross the Krishna-bead (the larger end-bead). Turn the mala around and chant back. The Krishna-bead is honored.
Brahma-muhurta — the 96 minutes before sunrise — is the most powerful time for chanting. If you can begin then, the rounds settle faster.
If you missed brahma-muhurta today, do not skip — chant now. The Name does not require a perfect time, only your presence.
items.source: Siksastakam 2 — kalau nāsty eva nāsty eva

items.tip: When tongue is dry and you are exhausted, the Name still lives in the heart. The chanting continues silently. Carry on.
When the heart is full of joy, slow down. The Name is asking to be heard, not finished. Do not rush past the gift.
When ill, lie comfortably and chant within the mouth. Sastra has no requirement for posture in illness. Continue the practice in whatever form you can.
The mouth chants for the ear. If the ear does not hear, the mouth is wasted. Chant slowly enough to hear each syllable.
Carry one line from yesterday's SB or BG class into japa today. Let the hearing feed the chanting.
Before chanting today, recall who Krishna is to you — father, friend, master, or beloved. Chant in that mood; the Name responds to relationship.
Today, ask only to remember Krishna's lotus feet. No other wealth, no other followers, no other liberation.
items.source: Siksastakam 4 — na dhanaṁ na janaṁ na sundarīṁ

items.tip: On Ekadasi, the Holy Name is said to have special potency. If a round was lost yesterday, add it today.
On Ekadasi, simplicity in food clears the mind. Light japa lands more attentively when the body is light.
